_comment: Maps each benchmark/cases/<CASE_NAME>/ to the independently-named extraction this run produced for it. Extraction names were chosen without copying the case's ground_truth.yaml name, so recall is scored on concept-match (same real-world thing modeled), not string-match. 'schema_type_match' records whether the extraction's schema.type family agrees with ground_truth.yaml's -- a stricter, separate metric from recall.

LEGAL_VSTART.note: Ground truth's schema (enum of stride types) doesn't obviously derive from its own description text either -- see README caveat.

RESERVED_VSET_X0X0_VLMAX_CHANGE.note: Same pattern as LEGAL_VSTART: ground truth's enum (never/always/custom) isn't clearly traceable to the description.

VECTOR_FF_SEG_EXCEPTION_PARTIAL_LOAD.note: Ground truth models this as an enum (no_subsegment_loaded/custom); extraction modeled it as boolean.

VFREDUSUM_INACTIVE_NODE_ELEMENT_BEHAVIOR.note: Near-identical enum values to ground truth (additive_identity/copy_through vs additive_identity/copy).

PMP_GRANULARITY.note: Same type, different encoding convention: extraction models raw G, ground truth models G+2.

MISALIGNED_MAX_ATOMICITY_GRANULE_SIZE.note: Ground truth is more precise (enum of specific powers of two); extraction only bounded minimum >= 0.

LRSC_MISALIGNED_BEHAVIOR.note: Ground truth has a third 'custom' option the extraction didn't include.

MTVEC_ACCESS.note: Ground truth models as a string enum (ro/rw); extraction modeled as boolean -- same information, different shape.

TIME_CSR_IMPLEMENTED.note: Slight framing difference: ground truth asks 'does it exist', extraction asks 'is it emulated' -- adjacent but not identical question.
